name: Mitochondrial Disease with Peripheral Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mitochondrial Disease Diagnostic Criteria with Peripheral Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of clinical signs and symptoms consistent with peripheral neuropathy (sensory, motor, or autonomic)
Evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction demonstrated by biochemical assays (e.g., decreased respiratory chain complex activity)
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear DNA mutations associated with mitochondrial disease
Electrophysiological evidence of peripheral neuropathy on nerve conduction studies
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-negative fibers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical peripheral neuropathy, biochemical evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction, and identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA or nuclear DNA mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, genetic, and electrophysiological data.

searchTerms: progressive nerve damage affecting sensation and movement
gradual loss of nerve function in limbs
muscle disease with ragged red fibers on biopsy
mitochondrial myopathy showing ragged red fibers
muscle weakness with abnormal muscle fibers
muscle weakness in hands or feet

common.symptomName: Sensory ataxia due to large fiber sensory neuropathy
searchTerms: loss of balance due to large fiber sensory nerve damage
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness
drooping eyelids and eye muscle weakness
tingling nerve pain in arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to auditory neuropathy

rare.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to mitochondrial dysfunction
searchTerms: blood sugar issues from mitochondrial dysfunction
diabetes linked to energy production defects

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate and pyruvate levels
Abnormal respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
imaging: Brain MRI may show basal ganglia or brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement
genetic: Pathogenic mitochondrial DNA point mutations or deletions
Nuclear gene mutations affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., POLG, MFN2)
other: Nerve conduction studies demonstrating axonal or demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily inherited peripheral neuropathy without systemic mitochondrial dysfunction
Absence of ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy
Autoimmune etiology with response to immunotherapy
Demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive peripheral neuropathy with multisystem involvement
Early onset of mitochondrial myopathy signs with neuropathy
Family history of mitochondrial disorders or maternal inheritance pattern
